Every test case in the [PR #1627](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1627) checklist now has a screen recording of the real Obsidian app, 55 clips in total, and every recorded check passed.

**How the clips were made:** I didn't use `dg-films`. It draws animated films and doesn't record the app, so its videos couldn't count as evidence. Instead, a small recorder captures the Obsidian window over CDP while each test runs. Each clip is silent, 4–16 seconds and about 120–330 KB. The red dot is the cursor, and input is slowed so you can follow it. The caption bar names the test case.

**What's covered:**
- **The 35 existing checks:** all re-recorded on `1c036bad`, and all pass. My first slowed-down version broke double-clicks, which made T5.2 fail, so I fixed the pacing and re-recorded that clip.
- **18 cases that had no test before:** a subagent wrote 20 new scenarios for them (P1–P18, with P5 and P6 split in two), and all pass. These cover:
  - the remaining ways to open the node modal
  - the Reading-view badge popover
  - "Add this relation to canvas", wikilink drag, and renaming a note while its canvas is closed
  - unlabelled relations, drag handles, and turning an arrow into a relation
  - group, nudge and duplicate, on straight and bent relations
  - SVG export

**Where they are:**
- In Roam, the discourse-dev-graph page **"Trang test"** has the branch block, then a run block "2026-11-15 · 1c036bad · obsidian-cdp video · PR #1627", then one block per clip using Roam's video embed.
- In the PR body, each checklist row under **Loom video** links its clips (`▶ T2.1`, `▶ P3`, …). GitHub only plays videos hosted on GitHub, so these links download the mp4 instead of playing inline.

**What the new scenarios couldn't do with real input:**
- **Cmd+G** opens Obsidian's graph view instead of grouping, so P14 groups through tldraw's Edit → Group.
- **Copy and paste over the clipboard** wasn't reliable over CDP, so P16 and P17 use Cmd+D. Clipboard paste of a relation is still untested.
- **Shift+Arrow** keys never arrived over CDP, so P15 nudges with 10 plain arrow-key presses.
- **P7** sets the relation type in the dropdown with a script, and **P9** starts the wikilink drag with a script, then drops it onto the canvas with real input.
- **Native menus:** the scenarios turn them off for the test and restore the setting afterwards. I checked that `app.json` is unchanged.
- **Not on `main`:** the P scenarios weren't run on `main`, so they check for no plugin errors and a sensible end state, not exact parity.
- **Two behaviours worth knowing:**
  - SVG export has no `@font-face` for the label's font. `main` behaves the same, because that font has no URL to embed.
  - An Obsidian tooltip error ("e.isShown is not a function") fires when the pointer passes over tldraw's resize handles. It happens on plain tldraw shapes too, so it isn't from this PR.

**Not recorded:** the popover position under a community theme or CSS snippet. It's still in the checklist for you to check by hand.

**Side effects:**
- **Test vault (Obsidian Vault):** the runs left test notes under `_verify/`, several new "Discourse Canvas" files, an image copy in the attachments folder, and new relations in `relations.json`.
- **Roam:** the 55 clips, plus one extra early sample I uploaded as a test, sit in discourse-dev-graph's file storage. Roam can't delete uploaded files.

input.new_string:
## Video evidence (Obsidian CDP) Use this when the PR needs recordings of real behaviour, such as in place of a Loom. Don't use `dg-films` for evidence: it renders drawn HTML films, not the app. ### Record - Wrap the scenario modules with `record.mjs` (in this skill dir) and run them through `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify`'s `run.mjs` from the worktree root: ```js import modal from "./s-modal.mjs"; import { recorded } from "/Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/record.mjs"; export default recorded(modal, { prefix: "a2-modal" }); ``` - Each `run()` becomes `local/pr-evidence/videos/-NN-.mp4`, or `$PR_EVIDENCE_VIDEO_DIR`. The clip is silent, 1600px wide, with a red cursor dot and the scenario name as a caption. Needs `ffmpeg`. - `recorded` slows mouse input and `client.evaluate` so viewers can follow. Press-to-press stays under tldraw's ~450ms double-click window. If a scenario only fails when recorded, suspect the pacing before the product. - Name scenarios ` ` (T2.1, P3, …). The ID is the slug, the caption, and the key in every later table. - Every recorded scenario still needs a real `expect`. A clip of a failing run isn't evidence: fix it and re-record. - Before uploading, check each clip by tiling one frame per clip (`ffmpeg -ss <70% of duration> … -vf tile=6x6`) and confirming the caption matches what's on screen. ### Upload - Upload each mp4 with roam-mcp `file_upload` (`graph: "discourse-dev-graph"`, `mimetype: "video/mp4"`). Call `get_graph_guidelines` once first. - Record `\t` in a TSV as you go. Build every later table and comment from that TSV, never by retyping URLs. - Confirm each URL with `curl -r 0-0` (expect 206). The URLs are public and served as `video/mp4`. - Put them on the Roam page with the same structure as above: `Trang test` → `` → `` → one ` {{[[video]]: }}` block per clip, in a single `create_block`. - GitHub only plays videos it hosts itself, so these links download the mp4. Say so in the PR body. ### PR body - **Verification** holds one collapsed `
` named "CDP scenario matrix with recordings". Columns: `Area | Scenario | Result | Video`. - The Scenario cell is a three-item list (HTML inside the table cell, `` instead of backticks): `
  • Scenario:

Driving Obsidian over CDP (found while recording ENG-2490 scenarios, 2026-11-15):

- Native context menus (macOS default) are invisible to CDP. Set `app.vault.setConfig("nativeMenus", false)` for the scenario and delete the key in teardown; verify `.obsidian/app.json` is unchanged.
- Native `<select>` popups can't be opened; set the value and dispatch `change`.
- Cmd+G opens Obsidian's graph view, never tldraw's group. Use tldraw's context menu Edit → Group.
- Shift+Arrow keydowns don't arrive; plain ArrowRight does (1px per press on the canvas).
- Clipboard copy/paste is unreliable (stale or image pastes). Prefer Cmd+D duplicate.
- Obsidian's tooltip throws "e.isShown is not a function" when the pointer crosses tldraw's aria-labelled SVG handles; it reproduces on plain geo shapes, so count it separately from plugin errors.
- Video recording of scenarios: `~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/record.mjs` (see [[reference_obsidian_cdp_driving]]).

For example, the popover line in `ModifyNodeModal.tsx` lists the 9 routes that show the popover (T2.1, T2.2, T2.6, P1–P4, P6a, P6b). The `intersectLineSegmentCircle` comment lists T8.5 and P17.

I skipped `eslint.config.mjs`, which doesn't affect the app at runtime. I kept `TldrawView.tsx` and the `relationUtils.tsx` header, even though their changes are comments only, and pointed them at the checks that still cover them (T9.1, T10.1).

**The `/pr-evidence` skill** (`~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/`) now covers video:
- **`record.mjs`** is the recorder, moved out of this session's scratchpad. Wrapping a scenario list with `recorded(scenarios, { prefix })` records each scenario to `local/pr-evidence/videos/`, which is gitignored. A smoke run on T2.1 passed and left the worktree clean.
- **SKILL.md** has a new "Video evidence (Obsidian CDP)" section with the rules from this session:
  - Don't use `dg-films` for evidence, because it draws the app instead of recording it.
  - Every recorded scenario needs a real check, and clips get a frame check before upload.
  - Upload with roam-mcp to discourse-dev-graph, and generate every table and comment from one TSV of IDs and URLs.
  - The Roam page follows the same branch → run → clip structure as the screenshots.
  - The PR body has one matrix with Scenario/WHEN/THEN bullets and a Video column, a "Not recorded" list, and a Loom section that points to the matrix.
  - The review gets one inline comment per runtime chunk, and each comment's line is checked after posting.

I also saved a memory note on what CDP can't drive in Obsidian: native menus, Cmd+G, Shift+Arrow and the clipboard, plus the Obsidian tooltip error that looks like a plugin bug but isn't. Future recordings won't have to rediscover these.
